content: 1. Tz G and Eichner M conducted a study on the control of onchocerciasis in Africa, focusing on threshold shifts, breakpoints, and elimination strategies. This research was published in the International Journal for Parasitology in 2011 (Volume 41, Issue 5, Pages 581-589). 2. Eyo JE, Onyishi GC, and Ugochukwu CU performed a rapid epidemiological assessment of onchocerciasis in a tropical semi-urban community in Enugu State, Nigeria. Their findings were published in the Iranian Journal of Parasitology in 2013 (Volume 8, Issue 1, Pages 145-151). 3. Fischer P, Yocha J, Rubbaale T, and Garms R utilized PCR and DNA hybridization techniques to confirm the absence of animal filariae in vectors of Onchocerca volvulus in Uganda. This study was published in The Journal of Parasitology in 1997 (Volume 83, Issue 6, Pages 1030-1034). 4. Gilbert C and Francis V summarized key highlights from the 7th General Assembly of the International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness, held in Dubai in 2004. Their report was published in the Community Eye Health Journal in 2004 (Volume 17, Issue 52, Page 66). 5. Guzman GE, Lavebratt C, Lujan R, and Akuffo H developed diagnostic methods for onchocerciasis using highly specific and sensitive native proteins. Their work was published in the Scandinavian Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2002 (Volume 34, Issue 8, Pages 583-590). 6. Kale OO, Bammeke AO, and Ayeni O evaluated the effectiveness of skin snip techniques for quantitatively assessing microfilarial densities of Onchocerca volvulus. Their findings were published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 1974 (Volume 51, Issue 5, Pages 547-549). 7. Lavebratt C, Dalhammar G, Awadzi K, and Akuffo HO assessed the field diagnosis of onchocerciasis in areas of high versus low endemicity using the Dot Blot Assay. This study was published in the Scandinavian Journal of Infectious Diseases in 1996 (Volume 28, Issue 1, Pages 75-81). 8. Nignan A, Millot G, Le Bras J, and Savel J developed an ELISA test for detecting Onchocerca volvulus antigenemia in skin snip-positive patients using monoclonal antibodies targeting a 56 kDa glycoprotein of Ascaris suum. This research was published in Acta Leidensia in 1990 (Volume 59, Issues 1-2, Pages 299-301). 9. Park J, Dickerson TJ, and Janda KD identified major sperm protein as a diagnostic antigen for onchocerciasis. Their study was published in Bioorganic & Medicinal Chemistry in 2008 (Volume 16, Issue 15, Pages 7206-7209). 10. Roffi J, Lafabrie B, Chovet M, Viale H, and Digoutte JP explored the detection of onchocerciasis using enzyme immunoassay (ELISA). Their findings were published in Médecine Tropicale in 1982 (Volume 42, Issue 3, Pages 297-306). 11. Klenk A, Geyer E, and Zahn H evaluated the sensitivity and specificity of purified Litomosoides carinii adult worm antigens for the serodiagnosis of human onchocerciasis. This study was published in Tropenmedizin und Parasitologie in 1984 (Volume 35, Issue 2, Pages 81-84). 12. Schlie-Guzman MA and Rivas-Alcala AR investigated antigen detection in onchocerciasis and its correlation with worm burden. Their research was published in Tropical Medicine and Parasitology in 1989 (Volume 40, Issue 1, Pages 47-50). 13. Taylor HR and Greene BM studied ocular changes associated with oral and transdermal diethylcarbamazine therapy for onchocerciasis. Their findings were published in the British Journal of Ophthalmology in 1981 (Volume 65, Issue 7, Pages 494-502). 14. Evans D, Alphonsus K, and Umaru J examined the ongoing transmission of onchocerciasis in central Nigeria, questioning whether the disease is being eliminated. Their study was published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2013 (Volume 89, Issue 5, Page 444). 15. Higazi TB, Mohamed H, and Zarroug I reported on the interruption of onchocerciasis transmission in the Abu Hamed focus in northern Sudan. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2012 (Volume 87, Issue 5, Page 195). 16. Katabarwa MN, Lakwo T, and Habomugisha P documented the elimination of onchocerciasis transmission in the Mt. Elgon focus of eastern Uganda. Their study was published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2011 (Volume 85, Issue 6, Pages 179-180). 17. Richards FO, Sauerbrey M, and Flores GZ provided an update on the Onchocerciasis Elimination Program for the Americas (OEPA). Their report was published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2011 (Volume 85, Issue 6, Page 188). 18. Rodriguez-Perez MA, Dominguez-Vazquez A, and Unnasch TR demonstrated the interruption of Onchocerca volvulus transmission in the Southern Chiapas focus in Mexico. Their findings were published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2013 (Volume 7, Issue 3, Article e2133). 19. Lindblade KA, Arana B, and Zea-Flores G documented the elimination of Onchocerca volvulus transmission in the Santa Rosa focus of Guatemala. Their study was published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2007 (Volume 77, Issue 2, Pages 334-341). 20. Vieira JC, Cooper PJ, and Lovato R evaluated the impact of long-term ivermectin treatment on onchocerciasis in Ecuador, highlighting the potential for infection elimination. Their research was published in BMC Medicine in 2007 (Volume 5, Article 9).
